import OAI.Algorithms.SubexponentialSAT.LeanCompat
import OAI.Algorithms.SubexponentialSAT.Incidence
import OAI.Algorithms.SubexponentialSAT.Types

namespace OAI.Algorithms

/-!
# Incidence slots and globally consistent factor words

Section 5.4 assigns each coordinate's incident factors to different slots.
The same factor word is then used at every incidence of that factor.  The
slot numbers themselves need not agree at different coordinates.

The ordered constructor and the slot-filling operations are computable.  An
additional constructor for arbitrary finite factor types chooses an enumeration.
No running-time bound or probabilistic independence assertion is hidden here.
-/

namespace SubexponentialSAT.SlotAssignment

open SubexponentialSAT.Factor SubexponentialSAT.Types

variable {V E : Type*} [DecidableEq V]

/-- The actual factors incident to one coordinate. -/
abbrev Incident (P : Pattern V E) (v : V) := {e : E // v ∈ P.scope e}

/-- An injective slot assignment separately at each coordinate. -/
abbrev SlotMap (P : Pattern V E) (Δ : ℕ) :=
  (v : V) → Incident P v ↪ Fin Δ

@[simp] theorem card_incident [Fintype E] (P : Pattern V E) (v : V) :
    Fintype.card (Incident P v) =
      (Finset.univ.filter fun e => v ∈ P.scope e).card := by
  exact Fintype.card_subtype _

/-- The incidence bound supplies exactly the cardinal inequality needed for slots. -/
theorem card_incident_le [Fintype E] (P : Pattern V E) {k Δ : ℕ}
    (hP : P.Bounded k Δ) (v : V) : Fintype.card (Incident P v) ≤ Δ := by
  rw [card_incident]
  exact hP.incidence_le v

/-- A finite slot assignment, using a chosen enumeration for each incident set. -/
noncomputable def slotsOfCardLE [Fintype E] (P : Pattern V E) {Δ : ℕ}
    (h : ∀ v, Fintype.card (Incident P v) ≤ Δ) : SlotMap P Δ :=
  fun v => (Fintype.equivFin (Incident P v)).toEmbedding.trans (Fin.castLEEmb (h v))

/-- Slot assignments exist for every bounded factor pattern. -/
noncomputable def slotsOfBounded [Fintype E] (P : Pattern V E) {k Δ : ℕ}
    (hP : P.Bounded k Δ) : SlotMap P Δ :=
  slotsOfCardLE P (card_incident_le P hP)

/-- For ordered factor indices, sort the incident factors and use their ranks.
This constructor makes the fixed local ordering in the exposition explicit. -/
def orderedSlotsOfCardLE [Fintype E] [LinearOrder E] (P : Pattern V E) {Δ : ℕ}
    (h : ∀ v, Fintype.card (Incident P v) ≤ Δ) : SlotMap P Δ :=
  fun v => (Fintype.orderIsoFinOfCardEq (Incident P v) rfl).symm.toEquiv.toEmbedding.trans
    (Fin.castLEEmb (h v))

import OAI.Algorithms.SubexponentialSAT.LeanCompat
import OAI.Algorithms.SubexponentialSAT.SubexpCountExecution
import OAI.Algorithms.SubexponentialSAT.SubexpTaylorExecution

namespace OAI.Algorithms

/-!
# Compile source rows into the represented counting input

The input records contain finite polynomial syntax for each row.  The
constructor below executes the represented compiler and Taylor shift to
produce every factor record.  No Taylor-array correctness premise is needed.
Scalar conversions remain parameters so concrete word encodings can supply
them without duplicating the source-data record.
-/

namespace SubexponentialSAT.SubexpCountSource

open SubexpLayoutSpec

variable {D p k Δ r : ℕ} {tau : ℚ} [Fact p.Prime]
  {F CK C : Type*} [Fintype F] [DecidableEq F]
  (S : Factor.System (Fin D) F (ZMod p))
  {c : Parameters p k Δ r tau}
  (L : Layout (E := SubexpActualRing.E p) S.toPattern c)
  (kops : SubexpSymbolicCost.RepresentedRing CK (SubexpActualRing.E p))
  (ops : SubexpSymbolicCost.RepresentedRing C (SubexpActualRing.Ring p (D + 1)))

local notation "A" => SubexpCounting.selectedLiftedLayout S L (D + 1) (Nat.succ_pos D)
local notation "coord" => SubexpActualRing.coordinateLift p (D + 1)
local notation "coordUnits" => SubexpActualRing.coordinateLift_unitDifferences p (D + 1)
local notation "sectionLift" => SubexpActualRing.residueSection p (D + 1) (Nat.succ_pos D)
local notation "baseMap" => LiftRing.of (SubexpActualRing.F p (D + 1))
local notation "labels" =>
  (fun i : Fin p => ops.decode (List.Vector.get
    (Prod.fst (SubexpTableExecution.labelsProgram ops.program p)) i))
local notation "labelUnits" => SubexpTableExecution.encodedIntegerUnits ops (D + 1)
  (Fact.out : p.Prime) baseMap _ (SubexpTableExecution.labelsProgram_correct ops p)

/-- Finite source data and local representation identities.  This record
contains neither precomputed Taylor arrays nor any counting-result premise. -/
structure SourceInput where
  node : Fin c.Q → C
  node_decode : ∀ t, ops.decode (node t) = (A).theta t
  enumeration : ∀ t, EnumerationData L t
  supports : Fin c.Q → Fin r → List (Fin D)
  supports_eq : supports = SubexpEnumerationCode.supportLists L
  outside : Fin c.Q → List (Fin D)
  outside_eq : outside = SubexpEnumerationCode.outsideList L
  bases : Fin c.Q → List (Fin D → ZMod p)
  bases_eq : bases = fun t => SubexpEnumerationCode.outerBases (enumeration t)
  increments : Fin c.Q → Fin r → List (Fin D → ZMod p)
  increments_eq : increments = fun t => SubexpEnumerationCode.innerIncrements (enumeration t)
  factors : List F
  factors_nodup : factors.Nodup
  factors_complete : ∀ e, e ∈ factors
  source : Fin c.Q → F → SubexpFactorCode.FactorSource D p r CK C
  scopeIndex : ∀ t e, Fin (source t e).arity ≃ {v // v ∈ S.scope e}
  color_eq : ∀ t e, (source t e).color = L.color e t
  table_eq : ∀ t e, SubexpTableInterpolation.tablePolynomial labels labelUnits

import OAI.Algorithms.SubexponentialSAT.LeanCompat
import OAI.Algorithms.SubexponentialSAT.SubexpMainLayoutChoices
import OAI.Algorithms.SubexponentialSAT.SubexpMainLayoutRows

namespace OAI.Algorithms

/-! Actual execution of the complete fixed Main layout phase. The row
suffix receives only bytes produced by the choices prefix. Its arithmetic
caches, Lagrange dictionary, and dense row table are generated by code. -/

namespace SubexponentialSAT.SubexpMainLayoutExecution

open BitProgram StructuredCalls SubexpMainProgram Subexp
open SubexpLayoutPorts (Allocation ordinary master)

attribute [local simp] Fin.coe_ofNat_eq_mod

variable {er es p r Δ R D : ℕ} [Fact p.Prime] [NeZero r]
variable {alloc : Allocation es} {a b : MainState er es}
variable {hr : 0 < r} {hQ : 0 < p^4 - 1}
variable {scopes : List (List ℕ)}
variable {hd : ∀ v : Fin D, IncidencePlanSpec.degree scopes v.val ≤ Δ}
variable {tables : List (List Bool)}

theorem choices_staticInputs
    (h : SubexpMainLayoutChoices.Result alloc a b p r (p^4 - 1) Δ R D hr hQ scopes hd tables)
    (hR : CounterPrograms.value (a.stacks (persistent es 25)) = R) :
    SubexpMainLayoutRows.StaticInputs (List.ofFn h.coefficients) h.packing.packing scopes alloc b := by
  constructor
  · exact h.prefixResult.scopeBytes
  · exact h.prefixResult.headers 3
  · exact h.packingOutputs 2
  · exact h.prefixResult.headers 0
  · exact h.prefixResult.headers 1
  · exact h.coefficientBytes.trans (CoefficientSearchProgram.encode_eq_valueWords p h.coefficients)
  · rw [h.prefixResult.persistent, hR, List.length_ofFn]

theorem choices_workspaceReady
    (h : SubexpMainLayoutChoices.Result alloc a b p r (p^4 - 1) Δ R D hr hQ scopes hd tables) :
    SubexpMainCacheSetup.WorkspaceReady alloc b := by
  intro i hi
  have hn := hi
  dsimp [SubexpMainCacheSetup.initiallyEmpty] at hn
  exact h.workspace ⟨i.val, by omega⟩ (by change i.val ≠ 254; omega)

/-- The numeric scopes contain only the chunk indices actually emitted by
the typed leaf's factor enumeration. -/
theorem orderedScopes_valid (x : SubexpLayoutConstruction.Inputs)
    (G : SubexpLeafData.Leaf (SubexpLayoutConstruction.variableCount x))
    (hG : (G.map ExecCNF.clauseSet).Nodup)
    (hell : 0 < CounterPrograms.value x.counts.ell)
    (hD : SubexpLayoutConstruction.dimension x = ChunkPartition.count
      (SubexpLayoutConstruction.variableCount x) (CounterPrograms.value x.counts.ell)) :
    ∀ C ∈ SubexpLayoutScopeOrder.orderedScopes x G hG hell,
      ∀ v ∈ C, v < SubexpLayoutConstruction.dimension x := by
  intro C hC v hv
  change C ∈ (SubexpLeafData.factors G hG).values.map
    (fun e => (SubexpLeafData.scopes G hG
      (ChunkPartition.indexEquiv _ _ hell) e).map Fin.val) at hC
  obtain ⟨e, _, rfl⟩ := List.mem_map.mp hC

/-- The canonical pack holds exactly 24,576 blobs. -/
theorem experts_bin_blobs : 48 * 512 = 24576 := by decide

/-- Geometry of an opened source: experts per layer and total blobs. -/
structure Src where
  nExpert : Nat
  blobs : Nat

/-- `FileExpertSource::blob`: the byte offset of `(layer, expert)`, or `none` for null. -/
def fileBlob (s : Src) (layer expert : Int) : Option Nat :=
  if layer < 0 ∨ expert < 0 then none
  else if expert ≥ s.nExpert then none

    let i := layer.toNat * s.nExpert + expert.toNat

  simp [fileBlob, h]

theorem fileBlob_expert_oob (s : Src) (l e : Int) (h : e ≥ s.nExpert) : fileBlob s l e = none := by

  split
  · rfl
  · simp [h]

  rw [Nat.add_mul, Nat.one_mul, Nat.add_zero]

  by_cases h1 : l < 0 ∨ e < 0
  · simp [h1] at h
  · simp only [h1, if_false] at h
    by_cases h2 : e ≥ s.nExpert
    · simp [h2] at h
    · simp only [h2, if_false] at h

    rw [Nat.add_comm, Nat.add_mul_mod_self_right, Nat.mod_eq_of_lt hb]

  split

    blobOffset bytes nE l e + bytes l ≤ layerOffset bytes nE (l + 1) := by
  unfold blobOffset
  simp only [layerOffset]

    rw [← Nat.succ_mul, Nat.mul_comm (bytes l) nE]

  omega

  induction m with
  | zero => have : l = 0 := by omega

  | succ m ih =>
    by_cases hl : l = m + 1
    · subst hl; exact Nat.le_refl _
    · have := ih (by omega)
      simp only [layerOffset]
      omega

    rw [ih', Nat.add_mul, Nat.add_mul, Nat.add_mul, Nat.one_mul, Nat.mul_comm b nE]

/-!
# MODULE: expert_dispatch_contract
SOURCES: include/strata/core/expert_source.hpp, src/core/expert_source.cpp
The adapter between `session_loop` and the CPU expert pool: per layer it validates geometry and
router ids, splits routed experts into GPU hits (rows zeroed) and CPU jobs, and latches failure.
Also the verify-window planner (`expert_pool_dispatch_multi`) and the hit Launch/Combine pair.

## Source semantics
* Clause 2: the router weight is never applied here; every job has `weight = 1`.
* Clause 3: `n_embd ≠ H` is refused (failure latched), never mis-indexed.
* `failed` LATCHES: once set, every later dispatch/hit call returns immediately without
  touching state, so a session cannot resume past a hole.
* The split: router index `i` is a hit (row zeroed, GPU owns it) or a job whose `slot = i`;
  `njobs` indexes jobs, `i` indexes output rows, and every row is written by exactly one side.
* `hits_ready` is all-or-nothing over the ten hit-path buffers.
* `Combine` adds `hit_out` only when `hit_pending` was set by `Launch`, and clears it.
* Multi-token: `first_of[i]` is the earliest entry with the same expert id; the PCIe share is
  `(nmiss * pcie_num) >> 8` of the distinct misses; entry `i` belongs to token `i / k`.

## Form template identifiers
`ExpertDispatch` → `Disp`; `expert_pool_dispatch` → `dispatch`; `ExpertJob` → job slot list
`jobs`; `is_hit` → `hit`; `hits_ready` → `hitsReady`; `expert_hit_run(Combine)` → `combine`;
`first_of` → `firstOf`; `pcie_num` → `pcieNum`.
-/

-- § dispatch state and failure latching

/-!
# MODULE: expert_cache_residency
SOURCES: src/core/expert_cache.cpp
The VRAM expert tier's residency table: compulsory-miss admission with no eviction, either from one
global counter or from per-layer slot ranges (R4.2g), plus slot addressing (uniform or 256-aligned
variable-size slots), fill-size clamping and the `STRP` profile reader's validation.

## Source semantics
* `layer_slot_range(l)`: `q = slots / n_layers`, `lo = l*q`, `hi = (l+1)*q` except the LAST layer,
  which takes everything up to `slots`; the ranges tile `[0, slots)` exactly.
* `admit` returns the existing slot when already resident (idempotent); otherwise the next free slot
  if one remains, else `kNotResident`.  There is no eviction: a resident slot never changes, and no
  two `(layer, expert)` pairs ever share a slot.
* `slot_of` / `admit` refuse out-of-range axes.
* `fill_slot` copies `bytes` if `0 < bytes ≤ blob`, else the whole `blob`.
* `open_sized` rounds every slot up to 256 bytes; offsets are the running sum.
* `read_expert_profile` refuses `n_ranked > slots` and any pair out of range.

## Form template identifiers
`ExpertCache` → `Cache`; `residency_` → `res`; `next_free_` → `next`; `slots_` → `slots`;
`admit` → `admit`; `layer_slot_range` → `lo`/`hi`; `fill_slot` byte count → `fillBytes`;
`open_sized` offsets → `slotOffsets`; `read_expert_profile` → `profileOk`.
-/

namespace Strata.ExpertCacheResidency

-- § per-layer slot ranges

/-- Lower end of layer `l`'s range. -/
def lo (slots nL l : Nat) : Nat := l * (slots / nL)

/-- Upper end of layer `l`'s range; the last layer takes the remainder. -/
def hi (slots nL l : Nat) : Nat := if l = nL - 1 then slots else (l + 1) * (slots / nL)

/-- The first layer starts at slot 0. -/
theorem lo_zero (s nL : Nat) : lo s nL 0 = 0 := by simp [lo]

/-- The last layer ends at `slots`: no slot is orphaned by the division. -/
theorem hi_last (s nL : Nat) : hi s nL (nL - 1) = s := by simp [hi]

/-- Consecutive ranges are contiguous: layer `l` ends where layer `l+1` begins. -/
theorem hi_eq_lo_succ (s nL l : Nat) (h : l + 1 < nL) : hi s nL l = lo s nL (l + 1) := by
  have : l ≠ nL - 1 := by omega
  simp [hi, lo, this]

/-- Every range start lies inside the arena. -/
theorem lo_le_slots (s nL l : Nat) (h : l < nL) : lo s nL l ≤ s := by
  unfold lo
  have h1 : l * (s / nL) ≤ nL * (s / nL) := Nat.mul_le_mul_right _ (Nat.le_of_lt h)
  have h2 := Nat.mul_div_le s nL
  omega

/-- Every range is well-formed (`lo ≤ hi`). -/
theorem lo_le_hi (s nL l : Nat) (h : l < nL) : lo s nL l ≤ hi s nL l := by
  unfold hi
  split
  · exact lo_le_slots s nL l h
  · unfold lo; exact Nat.mul_le_mul_right _ (Nat.le_succ l)

/-- Every range end lies inside the arena. -/
theorem hi_le_slots (s nL l : Nat) (h : l < nL) : hi s nL l ≤ s := by
  unfold hi
  split
  · exact Nat.le_refl _
  · have hl : l + 1 < nL := by omega
    have := lo_le_slots s nL (l + 1) hl
    unfold lo at this; exact this

-- § admission (global counter)

/-- Residency table (flat key `layer * n_expert + expert` ↦ slot) and the global free pointer. -/
structure Cache where
  res : Nat → Option Nat
  next : Nat
  slots : Nat

/-- `ExpertCache::admit` on the global path: existing slot, next free slot, or `none` when full. -/
def admit (c : Cache) (key : Nat) : Option Nat × Cache :=
  match c.res key with
  | some s => (some s, c)
  | none =>
    if c.next < c.slots then
      (some c.next, { c with res := fun x => if x = key then some c.next else c.res x, next := c.next + 1 })
    else (none, c)

/-- The cache invariant: assigned slots are below `next ≤ slots`, and the table is injective. -/
def Inv (c : Cache) : Prop :=
  c.next ≤ c.slots ∧ (∀ x s, c.res x = some s → s < c.next) ∧
    (∀ x y s, c.res x = some s → c.res y = some s → x = y)

/-- An empty cache satisfies the invariant. -/
theorem inv_empty (slots : Nat) : Inv ⟨fun _ => none, 0, slots⟩ := by
  refine ⟨Nat.zero_le _, ?_, ?_⟩ <;> intros <;> contradiction

/-- `admit` preserves the invariant: no slot is ever shared, none exceeds the arena. -/
theorem admit_inv (c : Cache) (key : Nat) (h : Inv c) : Inv (admit c key).2 := by
  obtain ⟨hn, hlt, hinj⟩ := h
  unfold admit
  split
  · exact ⟨hn, hlt, hinj⟩
  · rename_i hk
    split
    · rename_i hfree
      refine ⟨by simp; omega, ?_, ?_⟩
      · intro x s hx
        simp only at hx ⊢
        split at hx
        · simp at hx; omega
        · have := hlt x s hx; omega
      · intro x y s hx hy
        simp only at hx hy
        split at hx <;> split at hy
        · rename_i a b; rw [a, b]
        · rename_i a b; simp at hx; subst hx; have := hlt y _ hy; omega
        · rename_i a b; simp at hy; subst hy; have := hlt x _ hx; omega
        · exact hinj x y s hx hy
    · exact ⟨hn, hlt, hinj⟩

/-- A returned slot is always inside the arena. -/
theorem admit_lt_slots (c : Cache) (key s : Nat) (h : Inv c) (ha : (admit c key).1 = some s) :
    s < c.slots := by
  obtain ⟨hn, hlt, _⟩ := h
  unfold admit at ha
  split at ha
  · rename_i s' hs; simp at ha; subst ha; have := hlt key s' hs; omega
  · split at ha
    · simp at ha; omega
    · contradiction

/-- Admission is idempotent: admitting a resident key returns its slot and changes nothing. -/
theorem admit_resident (c : Cache) (key s : Nat) (h : c.res key = some s) :
    admit c key = (some s, c) := by
  simp [admit, h]

/-- No eviction: a resident key keeps its slot after any admission. -/
theorem admit_keeps (c : Cache) (key x s : Nat) (h : c.res x = some s) :
    (admit c key).2.res x = some s := by
  unfold admit
  split
  · exact h
  · rename_i hk
    split
    · simp only
      split
      · rename_i hx; subst hx; rw [hk] at h; contradiction
      · exact h
    · exact h

/-- A full cache refuses every non-resident key and stays unchanged. -/
theorem admit_full (c : Cache) (key : Nat) (hk : c.res key = none) (hf : c.slots ≤ c.next) :
    admit c key = (none, c) := by
  simp [admit, hk, Nat.not_lt.mpr hf]

-- § per-layer admission

/-- R4.2g: admission bounded by the layer's own range; returns the slot and the new pointer. -/
def admitLayer (ptr hiL : Nat) : Option Nat × Nat :=
  if ptr < hiL then (some ptr, ptr + 1) else (none, ptr)

/-- A per-layer admission stays inside that layer's range `[lo, hi)`. -/
theorem admitLayer_in_range (ptr loL hiL s : Nat) (hp : loL ≤ ptr)
    (h : (admitLayer ptr hiL).1 = some s) : loL ≤ s ∧ s < hiL := by
  unfold admitLayer at h
  split at h
  · simp at h; omega
  · contradiction

/-- The layer pointer never passes the layer's upper end once it starts below it. -/
theorem admitLayer_ptr_le (ptr hiL : Nat) (h : ptr ≤ hiL) : (admitLayer ptr hiL).2 ≤ hiL := by
  unfold admitLayer; split <;> simp <;> omega

-- § slot addressing and fills

/-- `fill_slot`'s byte count: the request if it is in `(0, blob]`, else the whole blob. -/
def fillBytes (bytes blob : Nat) : Nat := if 0 < bytes ∧ bytes ≤ blob then bytes else blob

/-- A fill never copies more than one slot. -/
theorem fillBytes_le (b blob : Nat) : fillBytes b blob ≤ blob := by
  unfold fillBytes; split <;> omega

/-- Round up to the 256-byte alignment `open_sized` uses. -/
def alignUp (x : Nat) : Nat := (x + 255) / 256 * 256

/-- An aligned slot holds its blob. -/
theorem le_alignUp (x : Nat) : x ≤ alignUp x := by unfold alignUp; omega

/-- Alignment wastes less than 256 bytes per slot. -/
theorem alignUp_lt (x : Nat) : alignUp x < x + 256 := by unfold alignUp; omega

/-- Aligned sizes are multiples of 256. -/
theorem alignUp_mod (x : Nat) : alignUp x % 256 = 0 := by unfold alignUp; omega

/-- Running offsets of `open_sized`: `off[0] = start`, `off[i+1] = off[i] + alignUp(bytes[i])`. -/
def slotOffsets (start : Nat) : List Nat → List Nat
  | [] => [start]
  | b :: bs => start :: slotOffsets (start + alignUp b) bs

/-- Every slot offset is 256-aligned when the arena start is. -/
theorem slotOffsets_aligned (bs : List Nat) : ∀ start, start % 256 = 0 →
    ∀ o ∈ slotOffsets start bs, o % 256 = 0 := by
  induction bs with
  | nil => intro start hs o ho; simp [slotOffsets] at ho; omega
  | cons b bs ih =>
    intro start hs o ho
    simp only [slotOffsets, List.mem_cons] at ho
    rcases ho with rfl | ho
    · exact hs
    · have := alignUp_mod b
      exact ih (start + alignUp b) (by omega) o ho

/-- The offset list has one more entry than there are slots (the end of the arena). -/
theorem slotOffsets_length (bs : List Nat) : ∀ start, (slotOffsets start bs).length = bs.length + 1 := by
  induction bs with
  | nil => intro; rfl
  | cons b bs ih => intro start; simp [slotOffsets, ih]

-- § profile validation

/-- `read_expert_profile`'s accept predicate on the header and ranked pairs. -/
def profileOk (nL nE want : Nat) (ranked : List (Nat × Nat)) : Bool :=
  decide (ranked.length ≤ want) && ranked.all (fun p => decide (p.1 < nL) && decide (p.2 < nE))

/-- An accepted profile never ranks more pairs than it has slots. -/
theorem profileOk_len (nL nE w : Nat) (r : List (Nat × Nat)) (h : profileOk nL nE w r = true) :
    r.length ≤ w := by
  simp only [profileOk, Bool.and_eq_true, decide_eq_true_eq] at h; exact h.1

/-- Every pair of an accepted profile is a valid `(layer, expert)`. -/
theorem profileOk_range (nL nE w : Nat) (r : List (Nat × Nat)) (h : profileOk nL nE w r = true) :
    ∀ p ∈ r, p.1 < nL ∧ p.2 < nE := by
  simp only [profileOk, Bool.and_eq_true, decide_eq_true_eq, List.all_eq_true] at h
  intro p hp
  have := h.2 p hp
  simpa using this

end Strata.ExpertCacheResidency

  two `(layer, expert)` pairs ever share a slot.
* `slot_of` / `admit` refuse out-of-range axes.
* `fill_slot` copies `bytes` if `0 < bytes ≤ blob`, else the whole `blob`.
* `open_sized` rounds every slot up to 256 bytes; offsets are the running sum.
* `read_expert_profile` refuses `n_ranked > slots` and any pair out of range.

-- § per-layer slot ranges

/-- Lower end of layer `l`'s range. -/
def lo (slots nL l : Nat) : Nat := l * (slots / nL)

/-- Upper end of layer `l`'s range; the last layer takes the remainder. -/
def hi (slots nL l : Nat) : Nat := if l = nL - 1 then slots else (l + 1) * (slots / nL)

/-- The first layer starts at slot 0. -/
theorem lo_zero (s nL : Nat) : lo s nL 0 = 0 := by simp [lo]

/-- The last layer ends at `slots`: no slot is orphaned by the division. -/
theorem hi_last (s nL : Nat) : hi s nL (nL - 1) = s := by simp [hi]

/-- Consecutive ranges are contiguous: layer `l` ends where layer `l+1` begins. -/
theorem hi_eq_lo_succ (s nL l : Nat) (h : l + 1 < nL) : hi s nL l = lo s nL (l + 1) := by
  have : l ≠ nL - 1 := by omega
  simp [hi, lo, this]

theorem lo_le_slots (s nL l : Nat) (h : l < nL) : lo s nL l ≤ s := by
  unfold lo
  have h1 : l * (s / nL) ≤ nL * (s / nL) := Nat.mul_le_mul_right _ (Nat.le_of_lt h)
  have h2 := Nat.mul_div_le s nL
  omega

  unfold hi
  split
  · exact lo_le_slots s nL l h
  · unfold lo; exact Nat.mul_le_mul_right _ (Nat.le_succ l)

theorem hi_le_slots (s nL l : Nat) (h : l < nL) : hi s nL l ≤ s := by
  unfold hi
  split
  · exact Nat.le_refl _
  · have hl : l + 1 < nL := by omega
    have := lo_le_slots s nL (l + 1) hl
    unfold lo at this; exact this

-- § admission (global counter)

/-- Residency table (flat key `layer * n_expert + expert` ↦ slot) and the global free pointer. -/
structure Cache where
  res : Nat → Option Nat
  next : Nat
  slots : Nat

/-- `ExpertCache::admit` on the global path: existing slot, next free slot, or `none` when full. -/
def admit (c : Cache) (key : Nat) : Option Nat × Cache :=
  match c.res key with
  | some s => (some s, c)
  | none =>
    if c.next < c.slots then
      (some c.next, { c with res := fun x => if x = key then some c.next else c.res x, next := c.next + 1 })
    else (none, c)

/-- The cache invariant: assigned slots are below `next ≤ slots`, and the table is injective. -/
def Inv (c : Cache) : Prop :=
  c.next ≤ c.slots ∧ (∀ x s, c.res x = some s → s < c.next) ∧
    (∀ x y s, c.res x = some s → c.res y = some s → x = y)

/-- An empty cache satisfies the invariant. -/
theorem inv_empty (slots : Nat) : Inv ⟨fun _ => none, 0, slots⟩ := by
  refine ⟨Nat.zero_le _, ?_, ?_⟩ <;> intros <;> contradiction

theorem admit_inv (c : Cache) (key : Nat) (h : Inv c) : Inv (admit c key).2 := by
  obtain ⟨hn, hlt, hinj⟩ := h
  unfold admit
  split
  · exact ⟨hn, hlt, hinj⟩
  · rename_i hk
    split
    · rename_i hfree
      refine ⟨by simp; omega, ?_, ?_⟩
      · intro x s hx
        simp only at hx ⊢
        split at hx
        · simp at hx; omega
        · have := hlt x s hx; omega
      · intro x y s hx hy
        simp only at hx hy
        split at hx <;> split at hy
        · rename_i a b; rw [a, b]
        · rename_i a b; simp at hx; subst hx; have := hlt y _ hy; omega
        · rename_i a b; simp at hy; subst hy; have := hlt x _ hx; omega
        · exact hinj x y s hx hy
    · exact ⟨hn, hlt, hinj⟩

/-- A returned slot is always inside the arena. -/
theorem admit_lt_slots (c : Cache) (key s : Nat) (h : Inv c) (ha : (admit c key).1 = some s) :
    s < c.slots := by
  obtain ⟨hn, hlt, _⟩ := h
  unfold admit at ha
  split at ha
  · rename_i s' hs; simp at ha; subst ha; have := hlt key s' hs; omega
  · split at ha
    · simp at ha; omega
    · contradiction

theorem admit_resident (c : Cache) (key s : Nat) (h : c.res key = some s) :
    admit c key = (some s, c) := by
  simp [admit, h]

theorem admit_keeps (c : Cache) (key x s : Nat) (h : c.res x = some s) :
    (admit c key).2.res x = some s := by
  unfold admit
  split
  · exact h
  · rename_i hk
    split
    · simp only
      split
      · rename_i hx; subst hx; rw [hk] at h; contradiction
      · exact h
    · exact h

/-- A full cache refuses every non-resident key and stays unchanged. -/
theorem admit_full (c : Cache) (key : Nat) (hk : c.res key = none) (hf : c.slots ≤ c.next) :
    admit c key = (none, c) := by
  simp [admit, hk, Nat.not_lt.mpr hf]

-- § per-layer admission

/-- R4.2g: admission bounded by the layer's own range; returns the slot and the new pointer. -/
def admitLayer (ptr hiL : Nat) : Option Nat × Nat :=
  if ptr < hiL then (some ptr, ptr + 1) else (none, ptr)

/-- A per-layer admission stays inside that layer's range `[lo, hi)`. -/
theorem admitLayer_in_range (ptr loL hiL s : Nat) (hp : loL ≤ ptr)
    (h : (admitLayer ptr hiL).1 = some s) : loL ≤ s ∧ s < hiL := by
  unfold admitLayer at h
  split at h
  · simp at h; omega
  · contradiction

/-- The layer pointer never passes the layer's upper end once it starts below it. -/
theorem admitLayer_ptr_le (ptr hiL : Nat) (h : ptr ≤ hiL) : (admitLayer ptr hiL).2 ≤ hiL := by
  unfold admitLayer; split <;> simp <;> omega

-- § slot addressing and fills

/-- `fill_slot`'s byte count: the request if it is in `(0, blob]`, else the whole blob. -/
def fillBytes (bytes blob : Nat) : Nat := if 0 < bytes ∧ bytes ≤ blob then bytes else blob

/-- A fill never copies more than one slot. -/
theorem fillBytes_le (b blob : Nat) : fillBytes b blob ≤ blob := by
  unfold fillBytes; split <;> omega

/-- Round up to the 256-byte alignment `open_sized` uses. -/

/-- An aligned slot holds its blob. -/

/-- Alignment wastes less than 256 bytes per slot. -/
theorem alignUp_lt (x : Nat) : alignUp x < x + 256 := by unfold alignUp; omega

/-- Aligned sizes are multiples of 256. -/
theorem alignUp_mod (x : Nat) : alignUp x % 256 = 0 := by unfold alignUp; omega

/-- Running offsets of `open_sized`: `off[0] = start`, `off[i+1] = off[i] + alignUp(bytes[i])`. -/
def slotOffsets (start : Nat) : List Nat → List Nat
  | [] => [start]
  | b :: bs => start :: slotOffsets (start + alignUp b) bs

/-- Every slot offset is 256-aligned when the arena start is. -/

    ∀ o ∈ slotOffsets start bs, o % 256 = 0 := by
  induction bs with
  | nil => intro start hs o ho; simp [slotOffsets] at ho; omega

  | cons b bs ih => intro start; simp [slotOffsets, ih]

SOURCES: src/core/pinned.cu
The pinned host arena (large pages, then `cudaHostRegister` of the whole range, else slice by
slice, else working-set locking) and the parallel chunked expert load with per-layer FNV-1a hashes.

## Source semantics
* `uniform_bounds(bytes, slice)` lists `0, slice, 2*slice, ...` while a whole slice fits, then the
  end of the last whole slice; with `slice = 0` it is empty.
* Sliced registration pins slices in order and STOPS at the first failure, so the registered
  region is always a prefix `[0, registered_bytes)`; the remainder `[registered_bytes, bytes)` is
  what the working-set lock covers.
* `load_experts_ranges` reads each layer in chunks of at most `chunk` bytes; the hash is carried
  across chunks, so chunking does not change it (FNV-1a is a left fold).
* `load_experts` lays layers out contiguously: layer `L` at `L * blobs_per_layer * blob_bytes`.

## Form template identifiers
`uniform_bounds` → `uniformBounds`; registration loop → `regPrefix`; `fnv1a64` → `fnv`;
chunk loop → `chunks`; `load_experts` offsets → `layerOff`.
-/

namespace Strata.PinnedArenaLoad

-- § uniform slice bounds

/-- `uniform_bounds`: slice starts, then the end of the last whole slice. -/
def uniformBounds (bytes slice : Nat) : List Nat :=
  if slice = 0 then []
  else
    let n := bytes / slice
    if n = 0 then [] else (List.range n).map (· * slice) ++ [n * slice]

/-- A zero slice size produces no bounds. -/
theorem uniformBounds_zero (b : Nat) : uniformBounds b 0 = [] := by simp [uniformBounds]

/-- Every bound lies inside the arena. -/
theorem uniformBounds_le (b s : Nat) : ∀ x ∈ uniformBounds b s, x ≤ b := by
  intro x hx
  unfold uniformBounds at hx
  have hd := Nat.div_mul_le_self b s
  split at hx
  · contradiction
  · simp only at hx
    split at hx
    · contradiction
    · simp only [List.mem_append, List.mem_map, List.mem_range, List.mem_singleton] at hx
      rcases hx with ⟨i, hi, rfl⟩ | rfl
      · have : i * s ≤ b / s * s := Nat.mul_le_mul_right _ (Nat.le_of_lt hi)
        omega
      · exact hd

/-- The bound list has `bytes / slice + 1` entries when at least one slice fits. -/
theorem uniformBounds_length (b s : Nat) (hs : s ≠ 0) (hn : b / s ≠ 0) :
    (uniformBounds b s).length = b / s + 1 := by
  simp [uniformBounds, hs, hn]

-- § sliced registration is a prefix

/-- Register slices `[bᵢ, bᵢ₊₁)` in order; stop at the first failure.  Returns registered bytes. -/
def regPrefix (ok : Nat → Bool) (acc : Nat) : List Nat → Nat
  | a :: b :: rest => if ok a then regPrefix ok b (b :: rest) else acc
  | _ => acc

/-- Registered bytes never exceed the last bound when bounds are increasing from `acc`. -/
theorem regPrefix_le (ok : Nat → Bool) : ∀ (bs : List Nat) (acc : Nat),
    (∀ x ∈ bs, x ≤ B) → acc ≤ B → regPrefix ok acc bs ≤ B := by
  intro bs
  induction bs with
  | nil => intro acc _ h; simpa [regPrefix] using h
  | cons a rest ih =>
    intro acc hb hacc
    cases rest with
    | nil => simpa [regPrefix] using hacc
    | cons b rest' =>
      simp only [regPrefix]
      split
      · exact ih b (fun x hx => hb x (List.mem_cons_of_mem _ hx)) (hb b (by simp))
      · exact hacc

/-- If every slice registers, the whole range up to the last bound is pinned. -/
theorem regPrefix_all (bs : List Nat) : ∀ acc last, (a :: bs).getLast? = some last →
    regPrefix (fun _ => true) acc (a :: bs) = (if bs = [] then acc else last) := by
  induction bs generalizing a with
  | nil => intro acc last _; simp [regPrefix]
  | cons b rest ih =>
    intro acc last hl
    simp only [regPrefix, if_true]
    have hl' : (b :: rest).getLast? = some last := by
      simpa [List.getLast?_cons] using hl
    rw [ih b last hl']
    cases rest <;> simp_all [List.getLast?]

/-- The locked remainder plus the registered prefix exactly cover the arena. -/
theorem lock_covers_rest (reg bytes : Nat) (h : reg ≤ bytes) : reg + (bytes - reg) = bytes := by omega

-- § FNV-1a and chunk invariance

/-- The 64-bit modulus. -/
def W : Nat := 2 ^ 64

/-- One FNV-1a step: xor the byte, multiply by the 64-bit prime, wrap. -/
def fnvStep (h b : Nat) : Nat := ((h ^^^ b) * 1099511628211) % W

/-- `fnv1a64(p, n, seed)` as a left fold over the bytes. -/
def fnv (seed : Nat) (bytes : List Nat) : Nat := bytes.foldl fnvStep seed

/-- The FNV-1a 64-bit offset basis used as every layer's seed. -/
def basis : Nat := 1469598103934665603

/-- CHUNK INVARIANCE: hashing two chunks with the hash carried equals hashing their concatenation. -/
theorem fnv_append (seed : Nat) (a b : List Nat) : fnv (fnv seed a) b = fnv seed (a ++ b) := by
  simp [fnv, List.foldl_append]

/-- Hashing any chunk sequence (carrying the state) equals hashing the joined layer. -/
theorem fnv_chunks (seed : Nat) (cs : List (List Nat)) :
    cs.foldl fnv seed = fnv seed cs.flatten := by
  induction cs generalizing seed with
  | nil => rfl
  | cons c cs ih => simp only [List.foldl, List.flatten, ih, fnv_append]

/-- The hash of an empty layer is its seed. -/
theorem fnv_nil (seed : Nat) : fnv seed [] = seed := rfl

/-- Every hash value fits in 64 bits after at least one byte. -/
theorem fnv_lt (seed : Nat) (b : Nat) (bs : List Nat) : fnv seed (bs ++ [b]) < W := by
  rw [← fnv_append]
  simp only [fnv, List.foldl, fnvStep]
  exact Nat.mod_lt _ (by decide)

-- § chunked reads

/-- Read sizes for `remaining` bytes in chunks of `c`: full chunks, then the tail. -/
def chunks (rem c : Nat) : List Nat :=
  List.replicate (rem / c) c ++ (if rem % c = 0 then [] else [rem % c])

/-- Sum of a replicated list. -/
theorem sum_replicate (n c : Nat) : (List.replicate n c).foldl (· + ·) 0 = n * c := by
  have : ∀ acc, (List.replicate n c).foldl (· + ·) acc = acc + n * c := by
    induction n with
    | zero => intro; simp
    | succ n ih => intro acc; simp only [List.replicate_succ, List.foldl]; rw [ih]; rw [Nat.succ_mul]; omega
  simpa using this 0

/-- The chunk loop reads exactly the layer's bytes. -/
theorem chunks_sum (rem c : Nat) : (chunks rem c).foldl (· + ·) 0 = rem := by
  unfold chunks
  rw [List.foldl_append, sum_replicate]
  have hd := Nat.div_add_mod rem c
  split
  · simp; rw [Nat.mul_comm]; omega
  · simp; rw [Nat.mul_comm]; omega

/-- No single read exceeds the chunk size. -/
theorem chunks_le (rem c : Nat) (hc : 0 < c) : ∀ x ∈ chunks rem c, x ≤ c := by
  intro x hx
  simp only [chunks, List.mem_append, List.mem_replicate] at hx
  rcases hx with ⟨_, rfl⟩ | hx
  · exact Nat.le_refl _
  · split at hx
    · contradiction
    · simp at hx; subst hx; exact Nat.le_of_lt (Nat.mod_lt _ hc)

-- § layer layout of `load_experts`

/-- `load_experts`'s layer offset. -/
def layerOff (blobBytes perLayer L : Nat) : Nat := L * perLayer * blobBytes

/-- Layers are contiguous: layer `L` ends exactly where layer `L+1` begins. -/
theorem layerOff_succ (bb pl L : Nat) : layerOff bb pl L + pl * bb = layerOff bb pl (L + 1) := by
  unfold layerOff; rw [Nat.succ_mul, Nat.add_mul]

end Strata.PinnedArenaLoad

## Source semantics
* `submit` rejects any request whose offset, length or buffer address is not a multiple of the
  sector alignment, and any zero-length request.
* Every accepted submit yields exactly one completion; POSIX completes inside `submit` and queues
  it, Windows queues read-at-EOF as an immediate zero-byte success.
* `wait(out, max)` drains queued completions first, FIFO, at most `max`, never losing one.
* A completion is ok iff its NTSTATUS is 0 or `STATUS_END_OF_FILE` (0xC0000011); POSIX: `got ≥ 0`.
* A `wake()` packet carries `WAKE_TAG` and is not a read.

## Form template identifiers
`DirectFile::submit` alignment check → `accepts`; `Impl::done` / `immediate` → queue `q`;
`DirectFile::wait` → `wait`; NTSTATUS check → `statusOk`; `Completion` → `Comp`.
-/

/-- `submit`'s precondition with sector alignment `A`. -/
def accepts (A offset length buffer : Nat) : Bool :=
  offset % A == 0 && length % A == 0 && buffer % A == 0 && length != 0

/-- An accepted request is aligned in all three coordinates and non-empty. -/
theorem accepts_spec (A o l b : Nat) (h : accepts A o l b = true) :
    o % A = 0 ∧ l % A = 0 ∧ b % A = 0 ∧ 0 < l := by
  simp only [accepts, Bool.and_eq_true, beq_iff_eq, bne_iff_ne, ne_eq] at h
  obtain ⟨⟨⟨h1, h2⟩, h3⟩, h4⟩ := h
  exact ⟨h1, h2, h3, by omega⟩

/-- A zero-length request is always refused. -/
theorem accepts_zero (A o b : Nat) : accepts A o 0 b = false := by
  simp [accepts]

/-- With 4 KiB sectors, an aligned request ends on a sector boundary. -/
theorem aligned_end (o l : Nat) (h : accepts 4096 o l 0 = true) : (o + l) % 4096 = 0 := by
  obtain ⟨h1, h2, _, _⟩ := accepts_spec 4096 o l 0 h
  omega

/-- A completion: tag, bytes transferred, success. -/

  tag : Nat
  bytes : Nat
  ok : Bool

  simp [wait, List.take_append_drop]

  simp [wait, List.length_take]

  simp [posixSubmit]

  have : ¬ (0 ≤ g) := by omega
  simp [posixSubmit, hg, this]

theorem drain_all (q : List Comp) (m : Nat) (h : q.length ≤ m) : (wait q m).1 = q ∧ (wait q m).2 = [] := by
  simp [wait, List.take_of_length_le h, List.drop_of_length_le h]

/-- `STATUS_END_OF_FILE`. -/

/-- A Windows completion is ok on success or a legal short read at the last page. -/
def statusOk (s : Nat) : Bool := s == 0 || s == STATUS_END_OF_FILE

/-- Exactly two statuses are accepted. -/

  simp [statusOk, STATUS_END_OF_FILE]

theorem statusOk_other (s : Nat) (h0 : s ≠ 0) (h1 : s ≠ 3221225489) : statusOk s = false := by
  cases h : statusOk s
  · rfl
  · rcases (statusOk_iff s).1 h with h' | h' <;> contradiction

end Strata.DirectFileReads

# MODULE: resident_memory_lock

Keeping the expert arena resident without privileges: on Windows, raise the working-set minimum by
the region plus a 512 MiB margin and `VirtualLock` it in 1 GiB chunks; on POSIX, one `mlock`.

## Source semantics
* Null pointer or zero bytes: nothing locked, `ok = false`.
* Windows: `new_min = min + bytes + margin`, `new_max = max(max, new_min + margin)`; then chunks
  `[off, off + min(chunk, bytes - off))`; `locked_bytes` is the end of the last successful chunk;
  a failure stops the loop with `ok = (off > 0)`; all chunks succeeding gives `locked = bytes`.
* POSIX: `mlock` is all or nothing: `locked ∈ {0, bytes}`.

## Form template identifiers
`lock_resident` (Windows) → `lockChunks`; working-set sizing → `newMin`/`newMax`;
`lock_resident` (POSIX) → `mlockResult`; `LockResult` → `(ok, locked)`.
-/

namespace Strata.ResidentMemoryLock

-- § working-set sizing

/-- The 512 MiB headroom. -/
def margin : Nat := 512 * 2 ^ 20

/-- Raised minimum working set. -/
def newMin (minWs bytes : Nat) : Nat := minWs + bytes + margin

/-- Maximum working set: kept if already large enough, else `new_min + margin`. -/
def newMax (minWs maxWs bytes : Nat) : Nat :=
  if maxWs > newMin minWs bytes + margin then maxWs else newMin minWs bytes + margin

/-- The minimum grows by at least the locked region. -/
theorem newMin_covers (m b : Nat) : m + b ≤ newMin m b := by unfold newMin; omega

/-- The maximum always leaves `margin` above the new minimum. -/
theorem newMax_ge (m M b : Nat) : newMin m b + margin ≤ newMax m M b := by
  unfold newMax; split <;> omega

-- § chunked VirtualLock

/-- The 1 GiB lock chunk. -/
def chunk : Nat := 2 ^ 30

/-- Lock `[off, bytes)` in chunks of `c`; `ok i` says whether the chunk at offset `i` locks.
Returns `(ok, locked)`; `fuel` bounds the number of chunks. -/
def lockChunks (ok : Nat → Bool) (c bytes : Nat) : Nat → Nat → Nat → Bool × Nat
  | 0, _, locked => (true, locked)
  | fuel + 1, off, locked =>
    if off < bytes then
      if ok off then lockChunks ok c bytes fuel (off + c) (min bytes (off + c))
      else (decide (0 < off), locked)
    else (true, locked)

/-- When every chunk locks and there is fuel, the whole region is locked. -/
theorem lockChunks_all (c bytes : Nat) (hc : 0 < c) :
    ∀ fuel off locked, off ≤ bytes → bytes ≤ off + fuel * c → (off < bytes ∨ locked = bytes) →
      lockChunks (fun _ => true) c bytes fuel off locked = (true, bytes) := by
  intro fuel
  induction fuel with
  | zero =>
    intro off locked h1 h2 h3
    simp only [Nat.zero_mul, Nat.add_zero] at h2
    simp only [lockChunks]
    rcases h3 with h3 | h3
    · omega
    · rw [h3]
  | succ fuel ih =>
    intro off locked h1 h2 h3
    simp only [lockChunks]
    split
    · simp only [if_true]
      by_cases hb : off + c ≤ bytes
      · exact ih (off + c) _ hb (by rw [Nat.succ_mul] at h2; omega)
          (by by_cases hl : off + c < bytes
              · exact Or.inl hl
              · exact Or.inr (by simp [Nat.min_def]; omega))
      · have hmin : min bytes (off + c) = bytes := by simp [Nat.min_def]; omega
        rw [hmin]
        cases fuel with
        | zero => simp [lockChunks]
        | succ f => simp [lockChunks]
    · rcases h3 with h3 | h3
      · omega
      · rw [h3]

  intro fuel
  induction fuel with

  | succ fuel ih =>
    intro off locked h
    simp only [lockChunks]
    split
    · split
      · exact ih _ _ (Nat.min_le_left _ _)
      · exact h
    · exact h

    lockChunks ok c bytes (fuel + 1) 0 0 = (false, 0) := by
  simp [lockChunks, hb, h0]

-- § POSIX mlock

/-- POSIX `lock_resident`: `(ok, locked)` from whether `mlock` succeeded. -/
def mlockResult (nonNull : Bool) (bytes : Nat) (mlockOk : Bool) : Bool × Nat :=
  if !nonNull || bytes == 0 then (false, 0)
  else if mlockOk then (true, bytes) else (false, 0)

    (mlockResult p b m).2 = 0 ∨ (mlockResult p b m).2 = b := by
  unfold mlockResult; split
  · exact Or.inl rfl
  · split <;> simp

    (mlockResult p b m).1 = true ↔ p = true ∧ b ≠ 0 ∧ m = true := by
  unfold mlockResult
  cases p <;> cases m <;> by_cases hb : b = 0 <;> simp [hb]

end Strata.ResidentMemoryLock

/-!
# MODULE: ple_row_reader
SOURCES: src/ngram/ple_reader.cpp
The asynchronous PLE table reader: turns 90-byte row requests into 4 KiB-aligned page reads
(deduplicated per page, sorted by offset), fronts them with a bounded 8-way set-associative row
cache, and tracks completion per ticket.

## Source semantics
* Row `r` lives at `at = table_offset + r * 90`; its read starts at `first = ⌊at / PAGE⌋ * PAGE` and
  has length `⌈(at + 90) / PAGE⌉ * PAGE - first`, i.e. one page, or two when the row straddles.
* Rows `≥ n_rows` are zero-filled, not read.  Cache hits are copied, not read.
* Rows on the same page share one job (length is the max); jobs are submitted in offset order.
* The row cache has `rows / 8` sets of 8 ways; a row maps to `mix(row) % sets`; replacement is
  round-robin per set; after `insert(row)`, `find(row)` succeeds.
* A ticket's `pending` starts at its job count and each completion decrements it; `collect` returns
  when it reaches 0.  Ticket ids skip 0 when the 32-bit counter wraps.

/-- Ways per set. -/

  keys : List Nat
  next : Nat

def WF (s : CacheSet) : Prop := s.keys.length = WAYS ∧ s.next < WAYS

theorem insert_wf (s : CacheSet) (r : Nat) (h : WF s) : WF (insertSet s r) := by
  obtain ⟨h1, h2⟩ := h
  unfold insertSet
  split
  · exact ⟨h1, h2⟩
  · refine ⟨by simp [h1], Nat.mod_lt _ (by decide)⟩

/-- After `insert(row)`, `find(row)` hits. -/

  obtain ⟨h1, h2⟩ := h
  unfold insertSet

  · simp only [findSet, List.contains_iff_mem]
    exact List.mem_set _ _ (by omega) r

theorem set_index_lt (m sets : Nat) (h : 0 < sets) : m % sets < sets := Nat.mod_lt _ h

theorem capacity_le (rows : Nat) : rows / WAYS * WAYS ≤ rows := Nat.div_mul_le_self _ _

/-- Pending jobs after `m` of a ticket's `j` jobs complete (saturating, as the source decrements only

def pending (j m : Nat) : Nat := j - m

/-- `collect` returns exactly when every job of the ticket has completed. -/

/-- A ticket whose rows were all cache hits or out of range has no jobs and completes at once. -/
theorem no_jobs_ready : pending 0 0 = 0 := rfl

def nextTicket (t : Nat) : Nat := if (t + 1) % 2 ^ 32 = 0 then 1 else (t + 1) % 2 ^ 32

/-- Ticket ids are never 0. -/
theorem nextTicket_ne_zero (t : Nat) : nextTicket t ≠ 0 := by
  unfold nextTicket; split <;> omega

/-- Ticket ids stay 32-bit. -/
theorem nextTicket_lt (t : Nat) : nextTicket t < 2 ^ 32 := by
  unfold nextTicket; split <;> omega

theorem jobs_le_rows (pages : List Nat) : (pages.eraseDups).length ≤ pages.length := by
  induction pages with
  | nil => simp [List.eraseDups, List.eraseDupsBy, List.eraseDupsBy.loop]
  | cons a l ih =>
    have := List.length_eraseDups_le (a :: l)
    exact this

/-- `PleReader::open`'s refusals. -/
def openOk (maxInflight tableOffset nRows fileSize : Nat) : Bool :=
  decide (1 ≤ maxInflight) && decide (maxInflight ≤ 1024) && decide (tableOffset + nRows * ROW ≤ fileSize)

/-- An opened table lies inside the file: every in-range row's bytes are readable. -/
theorem openOk_rows (mi off n sz r : Nat) (h : openOk mi off n sz = true) (hr : r < n) :
    off + r * ROW + ROW ≤ sz := by
  simp only [openOk, Bool.and_eq_true, decide_eq_true_eq] at h
  have : r * ROW + ROW ≤ n * ROW := by rw [← Nat.succ_mul]; exact Nat.mul_le_mul_right _ hr
  omega

/-- The slot slab is bounded: at most 1024 slots of two pages. -/
theorem slab_bound (mi off n sz : Nat) (h : openOk mi off n sz = true) : mi * 2 * PAGE ≤ 1024 * 2 * PAGE := by
  simp only [openOk, Bool.and_eq_true, decide_eq_true_eq] at h
  exact Nat.mul_le_mul_right _ (Nat.mul_le_mul_right _ h.1.2)

end Strata.PleRowReader

/-!
# MODULE: ngram_ple_hash
SOURCES: include/strata/kernels/ngram.hpp, src/kernels/ngram.cpp
The host-side PLE n-gram hash (sixteen row indices per token from the last three token ids), the
IQ4_NL row dequantisation with its split-half nibble order, and the head-slowest gather layout and
table geometry checks of `PleTable`.

## Source semantics
* `mixed_n = (ctx[0]*m[0]) ^ ... ^ (ctx[n-1]*m[n-1])` in wrapping uint64: XOR, not sum.
* Context: `ctx[0]` is the token; predecessor `s` back is `prev[n_prev - s]` (oldest-first input).
  A predecessor that is NULL (`< 0`) or EOS cuts, and the cut propagates to every OLDER position,
  which becomes EOS.  The token's own EOS does not cut.  Token id 0 is real.
* Heads `0..7` hash the bigram prefix, `8..15` the trigram; row = `mixed % vocab[h] + offset[h]`,
  where `offset` is the running sum of `vocab`, so each head owns a disjoint row range below
  `PLE_TABLE_ROWS`.
* IQ4_NL: codebook has no `-8` shift; byte `j` of a block carries elements `j` and `j + 16`.
* Gather: head `h`'s 160 values occupy `[h*160, (h+1)*160)` of the 2560-vector.
* Table check: alone in its shard the table must fill the data section exactly, else fit in it.

## Form template identifiers
`ngram_mixed` → `mixed`; context construction in `ngram_rows` → `ctx1`/`ctx2`; row index →
`rowIdx`; `ple_artifact_consts` → `vocab`/`offset`; `kIq4Nl` → `cb`; dequant index → `elemIdx`;
gather index → `gatherIdx`; table size check → `tableOk`.
-/

namespace Strata.NgramPleHash

-- § geometry constants

/-- `PLE_N_HEADS = (NGRAM_SIZE - 1) * HEADS_PER_NGRAM`. -/
theorem n_heads : (3 - 1) * 8 = 16 := rfl

/-- Sixteen 160-wide heads flatten to exactly `n_embd`. -/
theorem heads_fill_embd : 16 * 160 = 2560 := rfl

/-- One IQ4_NL row is 5 blocks of 18 bytes. -/
theorem row_bytes : 160 / 32 * 18 = 90 := rfl

/-- `NG_HIST = (PLE_CONV_KERNEL - 1) * NGRAM_SIZE`. -/
theorem hist_len : (4 - 1) * 3 = 9 := rfl

/-- `NG_HC_DIM = NG_HC * n_embd`. -/
theorem hc_dim : 4 * 2560 = 10240 := rfl

-- § the XOR mix

/-- The 64-bit wrap. -/
def W : Nat := 2 ^ 64

/-- `ngram_mixed` over the first terms: assignment of the first product, XOR of the rest. -/
def mixed : List Nat → List Nat → Nat
  | c :: cs, m :: ms => cs.zip ms |>.foldl (fun acc p => acc ^^^ (p.1 * p.2 % W)) (c * m % W)
  | _, _ => 0

/-- The bigram mix is the XOR of the two wrapped products. -/
theorem mixed_two (a b m0 m1 : Nat) : mixed [a, b] [m0, m1] = (a * m0 % W) ^^^ (b * m1 % W) := rfl

/-- XOR, not sum: two equal products cancel to zero. -/
theorem equal_terms_cancel (x m : Nat) : mixed [x, x] [m, m] = 0 := by
  rw [mixed_two]; exact Nat.xor_self _

/-- A sum would NOT cancel: the rival reading gives a different index (concrete witness). -/
theorem sum_differs : (1 * 3 % W) ^^^ (1 * 3 % W) ≠ (1 * 3 % W) + (1 * 3 % W) := by decide

-- § context construction with the EOS cut

/-- `PLE_EOS_TOKEN_ID`. -/
def EOS : Int := 248044

/-- Does a predecessor cut the context?  NULL is `< 0`; EOS cuts too. -/
def cuts (t : Int) : Bool := decide (t < 0) || decide (t = EOS)

/-- `ctx[1]`: the NEWEST predecessor `p1`, or EOS if it cuts. -/
def ctx1 (p1 : Int) : Int := if cuts p1 then EOS else p1

/-- `ctx[2]`: the OLDEST predecessor `p0`, EOS if it or anything newer cut. -/
def ctx2 (p0 p1 : Int) : Int := if cuts p1 || cuts p0 then EOS else p0

/-- The cut propagates forward: a cut at the newest predecessor makes the older position EOS. -/
theorem cut_propagates (p0 p1 : Int) (h : cuts p1 = true) : ctx1 p1 = EOS ∧ ctx2 p0 p1 = EOS := by
  simp [ctx1, ctx2, h]

/-- A missing predecessor (`TOKEN_NULL = -1`) is replaced by EOS. -/
theorem null_is_eos (p0 : Int) : ctx1 (-1) = EOS ∧ ctx2 p0 (-1) = EOS := by
  simp [ctx1, ctx2, cuts]

/-- Token id 0 is a real token, not a cut. -/
theorem zero_is_real (p0 : Int) (h : cuts p0 = false) : ctx1 0 = 0 ∧ ctx2 p0 0 = p0 := by
  have h0 : cuts 0 = false := by decide
  simp [ctx1, ctx2, h0, h]

/-- An older cut does not reach the newer position. -/
theorem old_cut_local (p1 : Int) (hp : cuts p1 = false) : ctx1 p1 = p1 ∧ ctx2 (-1) p1 = EOS := by
  simp [ctx1, ctx2, hp, cuts]

/-- The token's own value never cuts its context (only predecessors are examined). -/
theorem own_eos_no_cut (p0 p1 : Int) (h1 : cuts p1 = false) (h0 : cuts p0 = false) :
    [EOS, ctx1 p1, ctx2 p0 p1] = [EOS, p1, p0] := by
  simp [ctx1, ctx2, h1, h0]

-- § row indices and head ranges

/-- The artifact's sixteen head vocab sizes. -/
def vocab : List Nat :=
  [20000003, 20000023, 20000033, 20000047, 20000059, 20000063, 20000069, 20000077,
   20000081, 20000093, 20000107, 20000147, 20000153, 20000159, 20000161, 20000171]

/-- The artifact's sixteen head offsets, transcribed separately rather than derived. -/
def offset : List Nat :=
  [0, 20000003, 40000026, 60000059, 80000106, 100000165, 120000228, 140000297,
   160000374, 180000455, 200000548, 220000655, 240000802, 260000955, 280001114, 300001275]

/-- Running prefix sums. -/
def prefixSums : Nat → List Nat → List Nat
  | _, [] => []
  | acc, v :: vs => acc :: prefixSums (acc + v) vs

/-- The transcribed offsets ARE the running sum of the vocab sizes (the parity check's content). -/
theorem offsets_running_sum : prefixSums 0 vocab = offset := by decide

/-- The vocab sizes are not the arithmetic sequence `20000003 + 10 i` of the reference selftest. -/
theorem vocab_not_arithmetic : vocab ≠ (List.range 16).map (fun i => 20000003 + 10 * i) := by decide

/-- The last head ends inside the 320,001,536-row table. -/
theorem heads_fit_table : 300001275 + 20000171 ≤ 320001536 := by decide

/-- Row index for head `h`. -/
def rowIdx (mix v o : Nat) : Nat := mix % v + o

/-- A head's row lies in its own range `[offset, offset + vocab)`. -/
theorem rowIdx_in_head (mix v o : Nat) (hv : 0 < v) : o ≤ rowIdx mix v o ∧ rowIdx mix v o < o + v := by
  have := Nat.mod_lt mix hv
  unfold rowIdx; omega

/-- Every head's range ends where the next begins, so heads never collide. -/
theorem head_ranges_contiguous :
    ∀ h, h + 1 < 16 → offset[h]! + vocab[h]! = offset[h + 1]! := by decide

/-- Every row index of every head is inside the table. -/
theorem rowIdx_lt_table (mix h : Nat) (hh : h < 16) : rowIdx mix vocab[h]! offset[h]! < 320001536 := by
  have hv : ∀ h, h < 16 → 0 < vocab[h]! ∧ offset[h]! + vocab[h]! ≤ 320001536 := by decide
  obtain ⟨h1, h2⟩ := hv h hh
  have := (rowIdx_in_head mix _ _ h1).2
  omega

-- § IQ4_NL

/-- `kvalues_iq4nl`. -/
def cb : List Int := [-127, -104, -83, -65, -49, -35, -22, -10, 1, 13, 25, 38, 53, 69, 89, 113]

/-- The codebook is strictly increasing. -/
theorem cb_sorted : ∀ i, i + 1 < 16 → cb[i]! < cb[i + 1]! := by decide

/-- No `-8` shift in this ggml version: code 8 decodes to 1, not -7. -/
theorem cb_no_shift : cb[8]! = 1 := by decide

/-- Element index of nibble `hi` (0 low, 1 high) of byte `j` in block `b`: split halves. -/
def elemIdx (b j hi : Nat) : Nat := b * 32 + j + 16 * hi

/-- Every decoded element lands inside the 160-wide row. -/
theorem elemIdx_lt (b j hi : Nat) (hb : b < 5) (hj : j < 16) (hh : hi < 2) : elemIdx b j hi < 160 := by
  unfold elemIdx; omega

/-- The split-half layout is a bijection: distinct nibbles go to distinct elements. -/
theorem elemIdx_inj (b j hi b' j' hi' : Nat) (hj : j < 16) (hj' : j' < 16) (hh : hi < 2) (hh' : hi' < 2)
    (h : elemIdx b j hi = elemIdx b' j' hi') : b = b' ∧ j = j' ∧ hi = hi' := by
  unfold elemIdx at h; omega

/-- Byte `j`'s two nibbles are elements `j` and `j+16`, NOT `2j` and `2j+1`. -/
theorem split_not_interleaved : elemIdx 0 1 0 = 1 ∧ elemIdx 0 1 1 = 17 ∧ elemIdx 0 1 1 ≠ 2 * 1 + 1 := by decide

-- § gather layout and table check

/-- Head-slowest index of value `d` of head `h`. -/
def gatherIdx (h d : Nat) : Nat := h * 160 + d

/-- The gather writes exactly the 2560-vector, each slot once. -/
theorem gatherIdx_lt (h d : Nat) (hh : h < 16) (hd : d < 160) : gatherIdx h d < 2560 := by
  unfold gatherIdx; omega

/-- Distinct (head, value) pairs never share a slot. -/
theorem gatherIdx_inj (h d h' d' : Nat) (hd : d < 160) (hd' : d' < 160)
    (e : gatherIdx h d = gatherIdx h' d') : h = h' ∧ d = d' := by
  unfold gatherIdx at e; omega

/-- `PleTable::open`'s size check: exact fill when alone, otherwise fit at its offset. -/
def tableOk (alone : Bool) (nRows tOff have_ : Nat) : Bool :=
  if alone then nRows * 90 == have_ else decide (tOff + nRows * 90 ≤ have_)

/-- A table alone in its shard is accepted only if it fills the data section exactly. -/
theorem tableOk_alone (n t hv : Nat) (h : tableOk true n t hv = true) : n * 90 = hv := by
  simpa [tableOk] using h

/-- The original shard: 320,001,536 rows fill exactly 28,800,138,240 bytes after the header. -/
theorem original_shard : tableOk true 320001536 0 28800138240 = true := by decide

end Strata.NgramPleHash

# MODULE: ngram_ple_hash
SOURCES: include/strata/kernels/ngram.hpp, src/kernels/ngram.cpp
The host-side PLE n-gram hash (sixteen row indices per token from the last three token ids), the
IQ4_NL row dequantisation with its split-half nibble order, and the head-slowest gather layout and
table geometry checks of `PleTable`.

## Source semantics
* `mixed_n = (ctx[0]*m[0]) ^ ... ^ (ctx[n-1]*m[n-1])` in wrapping uint64: XOR, not sum.
* Context: `ctx[0]` is the token; predecessor `s` back is `prev[n_prev - s]` (oldest-first input).
  A predecessor that is NULL (`< 0`) or EOS cuts, and the cut propagates to every OLDER position,
  which becomes EOS.  The token's own EOS does not cut.  Token id 0 is real.
* Heads `0..7` hash the bigram prefix, `8..15` the trigram; row = `mixed % vocab[h] + offset[h]`,
  where `offset` is the running sum of `vocab`, so each head owns a disjoint row range below
  `PLE_TABLE_ROWS`.
* IQ4_NL: codebook has no `-8` shift; byte `j` of a block carries elements `j` and `j + 16`.
* Gather: head `h`'s 160 values occupy `[h*160, (h+1)*160)` of the 2560-vector.
* Table check: alone in its shard the table must fill the data section exactly, else fit in it.

## Form template identifiers
`ngram_mixed` → `mixed`; context construction in `ngram_rows` → `ctx1`/`ctx2`; row index →
`rowIdx`; `ple_artifact_consts` → `vocab`/`offset`; `kIq4Nl` → `cb`; dequant index → `elemIdx`;
gather index → `gatherIdx`; table size check → `tableOk`.
-/

namespace Strata.NgramPleHash

-- § geometry constants

/-- `PLE_N_HEADS = (NGRAM_SIZE - 1) * HEADS_PER_NGRAM`. -/
theorem n_heads : (3 - 1) * 8 = 16 := rfl

/-- Sixteen 160-wide heads flatten to exactly `n_embd`. -/
theorem heads_fill_embd : 16 * 160 = 2560 := rfl

/-- One IQ4_NL row is 5 blocks of 18 bytes. -/
theorem row_bytes : 160 / 32 * 18 = 90 := rfl

/-- `NG_HIST = (PLE_CONV_KERNEL - 1) * NGRAM_SIZE`. -/
theorem hist_len : (4 - 1) * 3 = 9 := rfl

/-- `NG_HC_DIM = NG_HC * n_embd`. -/
theorem hc_dim : 4 * 2560 = 10240 := rfl

-- § the XOR mix

/-- The 64-bit wrap. -/
def W : Nat := 2 ^ 64

/-- `ngram_mixed` over the first terms: assignment of the first product, XOR of the rest. -/
def mixed : List Nat → List Nat → Nat
  | c :: cs, m :: ms => cs.zip ms |>.foldl (fun acc p => acc ^^^ (p.1 * p.2 % W)) (c * m % W)
  | _, _ => 0

/-- The bigram mix is the XOR of the two wrapped products. -/
theorem mixed_two (a b m0 m1 : Nat) : mixed [a, b] [m0, m1] = (a * m0 % W) ^^^ (b * m1 % W) := rfl

/-- XOR, not sum: two equal products cancel to zero. -/
theorem equal_terms_cancel (x m : Nat) : mixed [x, x] [m, m] = 0 := by
  rw [mixed_two]; exact Nat.xor_self _

/-- A sum would NOT cancel: the rival reading gives a different index (concrete witness). -/
theorem sum_differs : (1 * 3 % W) ^^^ (1 * 3 % W) ≠ (1 * 3 % W) + (1 * 3 % W) := by decide

-- § context construction with the EOS cut

/-- `PLE_EOS_TOKEN_ID`. -/
def EOS : Int := 248044

/-- Does a predecessor cut the context?  NULL is `< 0`; EOS cuts too. -/
def cuts (t : Int) : Bool := decide (t < 0) || decide (t = EOS)

/-- `ctx[1]`: the NEWEST predecessor `p1`, or EOS if it cuts. -/
def ctx1 (p1 : Int) : Int := if cuts p1 then EOS else p1

/-- `ctx[2]`: the OLDEST predecessor `p0`, EOS if it or anything newer cut. -/
def ctx2 (p0 p1 : Int) : Int := if cuts p1 || cuts p0 then EOS else p0

/-- The cut propagates forward: a cut at the newest predecessor makes the older position EOS. -/
theorem cut_propagates (p0 p1 : Int) (h : cuts p1 = true) : ctx1 p1 = EOS ∧ ctx2 p0 p1 = EOS := by
  simp [ctx1, ctx2, h]

/-- A missing predecessor (`TOKEN_NULL = -1`) is replaced by EOS. -/
theorem null_is_eos (p0 : Int) : ctx1 (-1) = EOS ∧ ctx2 p0 (-1) = EOS := by
  simp [ctx1, ctx2, cuts]

/-- Token id 0 is a real token, not a cut. -/
theorem zero_is_real (p0 : Int) (h : cuts p0 = false) : ctx1 0 = 0 ∧ ctx2 p0 0 = p0 := by
  have h0 : cuts 0 = false := by decide
  simp [ctx1, ctx2, h0, h]

/-- An older cut does not reach the newer position. -/
theorem old_cut_local (p1 : Int) (hp : cuts p1 = false) : ctx1 p1 = p1 ∧ ctx2 (-1) p1 = EOS := by
  simp [ctx1, ctx2, hp, cuts]

/-- The token's own value never cuts its context (only predecessors are examined). -/
theorem own_eos_no_cut (p0 p1 : Int) (h1 : cuts p1 = false) (h0 : cuts p0 = false) :
    [EOS, ctx1 p1, ctx2 p0 p1] = [EOS, p1, p0] := by
  simp [ctx1, ctx2, h1, h0]

-- § row indices and head ranges

/-- The artifact's sixteen head vocab sizes. -/
def vocab : List Nat :=
  [20000003, 20000023, 20000033, 20000047, 20000059, 20000063, 20000069, 20000077,
   20000081, 20000093, 20000107, 20000147, 20000153, 20000159, 20000161, 20000171]

/-- The artifact's sixteen head offsets, transcribed separately rather than derived. -/
def offset : List Nat :=
  [0, 20000003, 40000026, 60000059, 80000106, 100000165, 120000228, 140000297,
   160000374, 180000455, 200000548, 220000655, 240000802, 260000955, 280001114, 300001275]

/-- Running prefix sums. -/
def prefixSums : Nat → List Nat → List Nat
  | _, [] => []
  | acc, v :: vs => acc :: prefixSums (acc + v) vs

/-- The transcribed offsets ARE the running sum of the vocab sizes (the parity check's content). -/
theorem offsets_running_sum : prefixSums 0 vocab = offset := by decide

/-- The vocab sizes are not the arithmetic sequence `20000003 + 10 i` of the reference selftest. -/
theorem vocab_not_arithmetic : vocab ≠ (List.range 16).map (fun i => 20000003 + 10 * i) := by decide

/-- The last head ends inside the 320,001,536-row table. -/
theorem heads_fit_table : 300001275 + 20000171 ≤ 320001536 := by decide

/-- Row index for head `h`. -/
def rowIdx (mix v o : Nat) : Nat := mix % v + o

/-- A head's row lies in its own range `[offset, offset + vocab)`. -/
theorem rowIdx_in_head (mix v o : Nat) (hv : 0 < v) : o ≤ rowIdx mix v o ∧ rowIdx mix v o < o + v := by
  have := Nat.mod_lt mix hv
  unfold rowIdx; omega

/-- Every head's range ends where the next begins, so heads never collide. -/
theorem head_ranges_contiguous :
    ∀ h, h + 1 < 16 → offset[h]! + vocab[h]! = offset[h + 1]! := by decide

/-- Every row index of every head is inside the table. -/
theorem rowIdx_lt_table (mix h : Nat) (hh : h < 16) : rowIdx mix vocab[h]! offset[h]! < 320001536 := by
  have hv : ∀ h, h < 16 → 0 < vocab[h]! ∧ offset[h]! + vocab[h]! ≤ 320001536 := by decide
  obtain ⟨h1, h2⟩ := hv h hh
  have := (rowIdx_in_head mix _ _ h1).2
  omega

-- § IQ4_NL

/-- `kvalues_iq4nl`. -/
def cb : List Int := [-127, -104, -83, -65, -49, -35, -22, -10, 1, 13, 25, 38, 53, 69, 89, 113]

/-- The codebook is strictly increasing. -/
theorem cb_sorted : ∀ i, i + 1 < 16 → cb[i]! < cb[i + 1]! := by decide

/-- No `-8` shift in this ggml version: code 8 decodes to 1, not -7. -/
theorem cb_no_shift : cb[8]! = 1 := by decide

/-- Element index of nibble `hi` (0 low, 1 high) of byte `j` in block `b`: split halves. -/
def elemIdx (b j hi : Nat) : Nat := b * 32 + j + 16 * hi

/-- Every decoded element lands inside the 160-wide row. -/
theorem elemIdx_lt (b j hi : Nat) (hb : b < 5) (hj : j < 16) (hh : hi < 2) : elemIdx b j hi < 160 := by
  unfold elemIdx; omega

/-- The split-half layout is a bijection: distinct nibbles go to distinct elements. -/
theorem elemIdx_inj (b j hi b' j' hi' : Nat) (hj : j < 16) (hj' : j' < 16) (hh : hi < 2) (hh' : hi' < 2)
    (h : elemIdx b j hi = elemIdx b' j' hi') : b = b' ∧ j = j' ∧ hi = hi' := by
  unfold elemIdx at h; omega

/-- Byte `j`'s two nibbles are elements `j` and `j+16`, NOT `2j` and `2j+1`. -/
theorem split_not_interleaved : elemIdx 0 1 0 = 1 ∧ elemIdx 0 1 1 = 17 ∧ elemIdx 0 1 1 ≠ 2 * 1 + 1 := by decide

-- § gather layout and table check

/-- Head-slowest index of value `d` of head `h`. -/
def gatherIdx (h d : Nat) : Nat := h * 160 + d

/-- The gather writes exactly the 2560-vector, each slot once. -/
theorem gatherIdx_lt (h d : Nat) (hh : h < 16) (hd : d < 160) : gatherIdx h d < 2560 := by
  unfold gatherIdx; omega

/-- Distinct (head, value) pairs never share a slot. -/
theorem gatherIdx_inj (h d h' d' : Nat) (hd : d < 160) (hd' : d' < 160)
    (e : gatherIdx h d = gatherIdx h' d') : h = h' ∧ d = d' := by
  unfold gatherIdx at e; omega

/-- `PleTable::open`'s size check: exact fill when alone, otherwise fit at its offset. -/
def tableOk (alone : Bool) (nRows tOff have_ : Nat) : Bool :=
  if alone then nRows * 90 == have_ else decide (tOff + nRows * 90 ≤ have_)

/-- A table alone in its shard is accepted only if it fills the data section exactly. -/
theorem tableOk_alone (n t hv : Nat) (h : tableOk true n t hv = true) : n * 90 = hv := by
  simpa [tableOk] using h

/-- The original shard: 320,001,536 rows fill exactly 28,800,138,240 bytes after the header. -/
theorem original_shard : tableOk true 320001536 0 28800138240 = true := by decide

end Strata.NgramPleHash

All eight modules compile cleanly with **no `sorry`, no `native_decide`, no errors and no warnings**, covering all 9 assigned source files in about 137 theorems.

**How they were checked.** I couldn't use Axle: it was unreachable from this machine (HTTP 000), and the request only had `__fill_in__` placeholders for its session cookie and CSRF token. Instead I installed Lean 4.15.0 from its GitHub release and compiled every file with plain Lean, no Mathlib. That is an older Lean than the 4.35.0 Axle would use. The proofs only use basic `omega`, `simp`, `decide` and induction, so they should carry over, but nothing has been checked on Axle itself.

**Two other differences from the instructions.** The bare repo at `/tmp/ref_Niko1221_Strata.git` doesn't exist here, so I worked only from the source pasted into your message. The `pr_*`, `sync_repo` and `einsteinos` services aren't available as tools here, so the earlier chunks' files weren't consulted. I cloned `openai/math` and modelled the proof style on it, with main theorems built from `have`/`obtain` and helper lemmas.

**Modules** (in `/mnt/user-data/outputs/`):

- **`ExpertBlobAddressing.lean`** (`expert_source.hpp/.cpp`) shows how a `(layer, expert)` pair becomes a blob offset.
  - The separate `expert ≥ n_expert` check is needed: without it, `(l, n)` lands on the same blob as `(l+1, 0)`.
  - Valid pairs never share a blob, and every blob ends inside the file.
  - `open` accepts a file only if its size is exactly `blobs × BLOB`, and the stated pack size `48·512·BLOB` is confirmed.
  - The arena's per-layer layout keeps blobs inside their layer, the registered (pinned) region is a prefix, and with equal blob sizes the arena layout matches the file layout.
- **`ExpertDispatchContract.lean`** (same files) covers the dispatch adapter.
  - Once the adapter fails, it stays failed through any later sequence of layers.
  - A wrong `n_embd` and an out-of-range router id are both refused.
  - Hits plus CPU jobs always equal `k`, job slots are distinct, and every output row has exactly one owner (GPU or CPU).
  - The ten hit-path buffers are all-or-nothing.
  - `Combine` never adds stale data and adds at most once per `Launch`.
  - In verify windows, `first_of[i]` is correct, the PCIe share never exceeds the misses, and each entry maps to the right token.
- **`ExpertCacheResidency.lean`** (`expert_cache.cpp`) covers the VRAM cache.
  - The per-layer slot ranges tile `[0, slots)` exactly.
  - Admission never puts two experts in one slot, is idempotent, never evicts, and refuses new experts when full.
  - Fills are clamped to one slot, slots are 256-byte aligned, and the profile reader's checks are modelled.
- **`PinnedArenaLoad.lean`** (`pinned.cu`) covers the pinned arena and the expert load.
  - The uniform slice bounds stay inside the arena, and sliced registration pins a prefix.
  - FNV-1a gives the same hash however the data is chunked, and the chunked reads add up to exactly the layer's bytes.
- **`DirectFileReads.lean`** (`direct_file.cpp`): only aligned, non-empty requests are accepted, each submit produces exactly one completion, `wait` never loses or reorders completions, and the status check accepts exactly success or end-of-file.
- **`ResidentMemoryLock.lean`** (`memory.cpp`): the working-set sizing leaves the stated margin, chunked locking locks the whole region when every chunk succeeds and never reports more than the region, and POSIX `mlock` is all-or-nothing.
- **`PleRowReader.lean`** (`ple_reader.cpp`) covers the PLE row reader.
  - Each row read is page-aligned, one or two pages long, covers the row, and fits the two-page buffer.
  - Rows on the same page share one job, and a row is found in the cache right after it is inserted.
  - Ticket ids are never 0, and a ticket completes exactly when all its jobs have.
  - The table must lie inside the file for `open` to succeed.
- **`NgramPleHash.lean`** (`ngram.hpp`, `ngram.cpp`) covers the n-gram hash and table layout.
  - The mix uses XOR, so equal terms cancel where a sum would not.
  - A NULL or EOS predecessor makes all older positions EOS, and token 0 is a real token.
  - The transcribed head offsets are exactly the running sums of the vocab sizes, each head has its own row range, and every row index is inside the table.
  - The IQ4_NL codebook has no `-8` shift, and byte `j` holds elements `j` and `j+16` (split halves); the head-slowest gather layout fills each of the 2560 slots exactly once.
